A 65 year old man was killed when the house he was in was swept into the Guadalupe River near Goat Creek Rd. in Kerrville. His body was recovered several miles downstream in the 300 block of Center Point River Rd.

events.title: Flash Flood near Lackland Afb
events.description: 1 death. Bexar County. Thunderstorms produced 3-6 inches of rain over the northern part of Leon Creek. This sent a flood wave down the creek and there was a 9-10 foot rise near Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland. A vehicle was trapped in the flood water on Hall St. at Leon Creek, and one person died.

events.title: Flood near Egypt
events.description: 1 death. Montgomery County. Lingering floodwaters remained after heavy rainfall, along with some reports of wrecks and high water in spots. The most significant report came from local broadcast news station. They reported that first responders received a call around 6pm that a 15 year old had gone missing after walking into floodwaters near a retention pond near Turriff Circle just west of The Woodlands. The 15 year old did not resurface. Boats and dive teams attempted to complete a rescue and discovered that the 15 year old had drowned.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Willis
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Montgomery County. A local news station published an online news story, indicating that a 75 year old man was killed after their pickup hydroplaned in heavy rainfall along I-45 southbound between Shepherd Hill Road and Calvary Road.

events.title: Flash Flood near Bandera Flying L Arp
events.description: 1 death. Bandera County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. A vehicle was swept away at the 1500 block of Lower Mason Creek Rd. into Mason Creek. One person was found dead in the vehicle approximately two miles downstream.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Austin
events.description: 1 death. Travis County. A pecan tree was downed onto a restaurant patio along Barton Springs Road by strong winds produced by a line of thunderstorms. One man died after sustaining critical injuries from the falling tree.

events.title: Flash Flood near San Antonio
events.description: 1 death. Bexar County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding sending San Pedro Creek out of its banks near Furnish Ave. and S. San Marcos St. San Antonio firefighters were called to the scene to execute a high-water rescue. They recovered a man, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. Police stated a jogger or walker was pulled into the creek by the high water.

events.title: Lightning near Colleyville
events.description: 2 deaths. Tarrant County. Lightning started a house fire in Colleyville that was contained to the attic of the home, however a female adult and a child under the age of 3 died in the fire. Another child was transported with injuries.

events.title: Flood near San Antonio
events.description: 1 death. Bexar County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain Monday and Monday night across the northeast side of San Antonio. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain occurred. This caused a quick rise into flood stage on Salado Creek early Tuesday morning. A 44 year old man was killed by the flood waters in the Salado Creek Greenway, near J Street Park. Authorities were not able to determine how the man got into the water, but was suspected of being homeless and living near the creek.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Iowa Park
events.description: 2 deaths (indirect). Wichita County. A tractor-trailer was overturned (and rolled) on U.S. Highway 287 due to thunderstorm winds. Details on this event were relayed through local broadcast media.

events.title: Flash Flood near Sat Twin Oaks Arpt
events.description: 2 deaths. Bexar County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. The bodies of two homeless individuals were recovered from Salado Creek near Maltsberger Ln. in northern San Antonio. Law enforcement officials believe they were swept away from a homeless encampment in a drainage channel near the creek.

events.title: Flash Flood near Smithwick
events.description: 1 death. Burnet County. Slow-moving thunderstorms produced 8-10 inches of rain over the headwaters of Cow Creek. Washouts occurred along CR 328/Cow Creek Rd. both along and over Cow Creek at multiple locations. A 66-year-old firefighter and his emergency vehicle were swept away while responding to flooding along Cow Creek near FM 1174. His vehicle was found 2 miles downstream mangled and entrenched within flood debris and sediment, but his body had not been recovered as of the time of this writing.

events.title: Flash Flood near Travis Peak
events.description: 1 death. Travis County. Slow-moving thunderstorms produced 8-10 inches of rain over the headwaters of Cow Creek. The FM 1431 bridge across Cow Creek was destroyed with the main bridge structure collapsing and fragmenting into at least four segments. A minivan with six occupants was swept into the creek at the crossing at around 4 AM. One of the occupants, a 17-year-old girl, was able to open the car doors and get the others to safety but died in the flooding. Her sister was also swept into the creek but survived. The Emergency Manager estimated public property and infrastructure damage at $5 million across the…

events.title: Flash Flood near Sudduth
events.description: 1 death. Burnet County. Slow-moving thunderstorms brought heavy rain for several hours to Burnet on the morning of July 5. Burnet Municipal Airport reported 8.67 inches of rain. An LCRA gauge in Burnet reported 11.67 inches. The torrential rainfall caused the rapid rise of Hamilton Creek. A 22 year old man commuting through Burnet was swept off the road at Park Road 4 and US 281 into Honey Creek, a tributary of Hamilton Creek. His body was recovered 8 miles downstream.

events.title: Flash Flood near Marble Falls
events.description: 1 death. Burnet County. Heavy rain from slow-moving thunderstorms fell into the Hamilton Creek watershed contributing to a rapid rise of the creek that moved downstream near Marble Falls into the Colorado River. While only 1 to 2 inches of rain fell over Marble Falls, a swath of over 10 inches of rain occurred within the watershed upstream. An LCRA stream gauge on Hamilton Creek near Marble Falls measured a rise of 18.65 ft in about 90 minutes with 49,970 cfs before the gauge stopped reporting data. events.title: Flash Flood near San Angelo
events.description: 1 death. Tom Green County. Law enforcement reported flash flooding at the intersection of Coke Street and Schroeder Street which resulted in one fatality when a vehicle was swept away by the flood waters.

The flood wave moved downstream from Hunt to Kerrville. An NWS Flood Survey team found water in some houses along the Guadalupe downstream of Hunt reached eight feet. Numerous homes were flooded in the Bumble Bee Hills subdivision. Water reached as high as 5.5 feet in houses. The Cade Loop bridge over the Guadalupe was shifted by flood water. events.description: 10 deaths. Kerr County. There was catastrophic and deadly flash flooding along the Guadalupe River after around ten inches of rain fell in approximately four hours over the headwaters of the river. The flood wave moved downstream from Kerrville to the Kendall County line. In Kerrville, most of the homes on Loop 13 were flooded, debris damaged the guardrail on the G St. bridge, and an apartment complex and cottages along G St. E. were damaged or destroyed by flood water. events.title: Flash Flood near Longhorn
events.description: 11 deaths. Bexar County. Training of thunderstorms with intense rainfall rates produced a swath of 3-8 inches of rain across San Antonio. Several vehicles were swept off the Loop 410 access road into Beitel Creek. There were 11 fatalities in this creek and the surrounding area. Ten people were rescued from the water, and two others were able to get to safety on their own. Damage from the flooding totaled $23 million across Bexar County.

events.title: Flash Flood near Sat Twin Oaks Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Bexar County. Training of thunderstorms with intense rainfall rates produced a swath of 3-8 inches of rain across San Antonio. A non-vehicle related fatality was reported near Wurzbach Pkwy and Salado Creek. The body was discovered on June 14th. The exact location of where this person went into the water is not known.

events.title: Flash Flood near (skf)kelly Afb San A
events.description: 1 death. Bexar County. Training of thunderstorms with intense rainfall rates produced a swath of 3-8 inches of rain in San Antonio. A vehicle was swept into Leon Creek near Callaghan Rd. and Hwy 90 and the driver died. The vehicle was discovered on June 14th.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Pittsburg
events.description: 1 death. Camp County. Tree downed onto a manufactured home southwest of Pittsburg.

events.title: Lightning near Gunter
events.description: 1 death. Grayson County. Broadcast media reported that two men were struck by lightning at The Bridges golf course in Gunter. One man was killed and another injured.

events.title: Flash Flood near Alpha
events.description: 1 death. Dallas County. Fire Department reported that two vehicles were submerged in high water near 12900 Park Central Drive at the LBJ bridge. One person was killed.

events.title: Flash Flood near Austin Mabry
events.description: 1 death. Travis County. Flash flooding occurred across the city of Austin with 6 water rescues reported, some of which included vehicles. On the 2200 Block of Hancock Drive near the Yarborough Branch of the Austin Public Library, an unhoused individual was swept away when Hancock Creek flooded. The body of the person was recovered downstream.

events.title: Flash Flood near Eagle Pass Muni Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Maverick County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Eagle Pass. There was water in homes and high water vehicle rescues. One vehicle was swept into a canal near Roosevelt St. and Austin St. The car became lodged under a bridge at Wilson St. The lone occupant, an 18 year old male, was found deceased in the Rio Grande River, just south of International Bridge II.

events.title: Lightning near Sebastian
events.description: 2 deaths. Willacy County. The Cameron County Office of Emergency Management reported a trailer home struck by lightning with the entire building consumed by the flames after the pre-dawn strike. Two residents inside were killed by the ensuing fire.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Ennis Muni Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Ellis County. A RV was blown over and rolled several times at the Texas Motorplex near Ennis. One man was killed and 4 others were injured.

events.title: Flood near Sherman Muni Arpt
events.description: 2 deaths. Grayson County. Two fatalities occurred when their SUV hydroplaned off of the US 75 service road and ended up overturned in a flooded drainage culvert. The two individuals were swept away into Post Oak Creek.

events.title: Flash Flood near Mico
events.description: 1 death. Medina County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Medina County 911 Dispatch received a call from an individual who was trapped in their vehicle that had been swept off Park Road 37 in high water at Mescal Creek. On the afternoon of the 5th, the vehicle was located about one mile downstream and the body of the driver 3-4 miles downstream just south of the Park Rd 37/FM 1283 intersection in Bandera County. The driver was a 20 year old male.

events.title: Flash Flood near Miles
events.description: 1 death. Runnels County. Law Enforcement received a call of a fatality from flash flooding. A man was swept away by swiftly flowing water.

events.title: Lightning near Bryan Coulter Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Brazos County. A 7 year-old girl was killed by a lightning strike outside of her home located between Bryan and Wickson Valley as a thunderstorm moved through the area.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Cedar Mills
events.description: 1 death. Grayson County. A boat with 8 people on board capsized in thunderstorm winds resulting in the fatality of a 6 year old boy.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Ben Wheeler
events.description: 1 death. Van Zandt County. A survey team confirmed a swath of straight-line wind damage likely associated with the rear flank downdraft of a previously tornadic supercell thunderstorm. A broad area of tree damage was observed between Ben Wheeler and Edom, and also east of Edom along FM 279. The most significant damage was confined to FM 279 where many trees were uprooted, including a few large trees. This damage was consistent with 75-80 mph straight-line winds, though saturated soils were likely a contributing factor. Sporadic tree damage was also observed along State Highway 64. events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Egypt
events.description: 1 death. Montgomery County. A home under construction collapsed due to strong thunderstorm winds. One worker that was inside was trapped and killed.

This is segment #2 of 4 of a multi-segmented EF-3 supercellular tornado that began in Montague County, crossed into Cooke County, Denton County, and then back into Cooke County. The tornado was ongoing for about an hour and a half with a total path length just under 48 miles. The tornado was the strongest in Cooke County and resulted in 7 fatalities in Cooke County. ||The tornado entered Cooke County at 1008 pm CDT time and exited into Denton County at 1049 pm CDT for a total path length of 25.41 miles. events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Northline Terrace
events.description: 8 deaths (4 direct, 4 indirect). Harris County. Nine total fatalities occurred due to the derecho across the City of Houston. One was from a fire from a lightning strike which is entered separately.

events.title: Lightning near Houston Weiser Arpt
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Harris County. Lighting fire destroyed a mobile home. One fatality resulted.

events.title: Flash Flood near Retta
events.description: 1 death. Johnson County. A vehicle occupied by two adults and one 5 year old boy was stranded in swift water off of CR 528. A witness saw the occupants get out of the vehicle and attempt to get to dry ground on foot when all are swept into the flood waters. Responders arrived and began searching for the victims. The adults were found and rescued around 5am and transported to the hospital. The 5 year old victim was found deceased in the water around 7:20am.

events.title: Lightning near Grangerland
events.description: 1 death. Montgomery County. Man was electrocuted while attempting to place a tarp over vehicles during a storm.

events.title: Tornado near Pagoda
events.description: 1 death. Trinity County. A short-lived EF1 tornado with maximum estimated winds of 100 mph impacted the Rock Creek Subdivision in Trinity. The tornado destroyed a mobile home in the subdivision, and two of its occupants sustained injuries. One of those injured died five days later. Widespread tree damage and damage to vehicles was also observed along an approximate 500 yard long and 200 yard wide path.

events.title: Flash Flood near (tpl)temple Muni Arp
events.description: 1 death. Bell County. Emergency management reported multiple swift water rescues overnight in Temple including one that resulted in a fatality after a woman's vehicle was swept off the road at a low water crossing at Pepper Creek.

events.title: Flash Flood near Woodlake
events.description: 1 death. Trinity County. Flash flooding resulted flooding along Piney Creek Road near Groveton. A man drowned in the floodwaters when attempting to retrieve items from his stranded car. Time was estimated based on radar and nearby flood reports as the man's body was not found until the next day.

The tornado then tracked to the south through open country until it reached just north of Farm to Market Road 94 where it damaged a few power poles. It then traveled to the south-southeast where it destroyed a house on the far north side of the city. Three vehicles at this residence were rolled at least a few hundred yards away from the house with two of the vehicles unable to be located. events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Beach
events.description: 2 deaths. Montgomery County. Strong thunderstorm wind gusts blew down the frame of a house under construction in Conroe, resulting in the death of two workers and seven injuries.

events.title: Lightning near West Womack Arpt
events.description: 2 deaths. Bosque County. A father and his son were struck by lightning walking home from the bus stop. The father died the same day but the son died weeks later, in June.

events.title: Tornado near Bayside
events.description: 1 death. Cameron County. A rapidly-developing mini-supercell formed ahead of an approaching squall line near the Lower Texas coast just before 4 AM Saturday, May 13. The supercell spawned a quick spin-up tornado that struck the town of Laguna Heights, Texas, over a two-minute period before the circulation moved over Laguna Madre Bay and rapidly dissipated. The tornado tracked to the east-northeast after the circulation was impacted by the approaching squall line, creating a boomerang effect since the original motion of the radar couplet was to the north-northwest prior to touchdown. events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Spring Skyline Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Harris County. Law enforcement reported that a tree fell on a vehicle near the intersection of East Cypresswood Dr and Whitewood Dr. One fatality was reported.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Frankston
events.description: 2 deaths. Anderson County. Tree and roof damage was reported throughout the Frankston area. The roof of a restaurant was also damaged including loss of shingles, partial decking removal and collapse of portions of the awning. One tree fell onto a manufactured house, killing two adults in the home. A post event assessment determined 70-90 mph winds caused the damage.

events.title: Flash Flood near Lybrand
events.description: 1 death. Hunt County. Brushy Creek overflowed Interstate 30 near FM 1565 and several cars were stuck in high water. The fast moving water swept one car off the road on the north service road and unfortunately the elderly man drowned.

events.title: Tornado near Cason
events.description: 1 death. Morris County. The supercell thunderstorm which produced a brief and weak tornado in eastern Camp County then went on to produce a stronger and longer-lasting tornado from southwestern Morris County and into northwestern Cass County. This EF-3 tornado with estimated maximum winds of 155 mph initially started along FM-144 south of the Cason community and very quickly became quite destructive, producing EF-3 damage to a home, and EF-2 damage to multiple structures before tracking northeast to Texas Highway 11. A few mobile homes were destroyed near the start of the tornado which resulted in several injuries.…

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Roscoe
events.description: 1 death. Nolan County. The Nolan County Sheriff confirmed 6 accidents on I-20 near Roscoe, with 1 fatality caused by a tanker truck rolling over. Also, several jack-knifed 18-wheelers. No tornadoes reported. but locally strong winds were reported. Also, multiple power lines were blown down nearby.

events.title: Flash Flood near Mesquite
events.description: 1 death. Dallas County. Broadcast media reported that a woman was found dead after her car was swept away by flood waters of South Mesquite Creek along the service road of Loop 635.

events.title: Flood near Webb
events.description: 1 death. Tarrant County. A man drowned when his car was swept off the road in the vicinity of a low water crossing near the 7000 Block of Webb Ferrell Road in Arlington, TX.

events.title: Flood near Lewisville
events.description: 1 death. Denton County. Broadcast media reported that a woman drowned after waters rose in a ravine that she and her husband were located in near the intersection of Southwest Parkway and Bellaire Blvd in Lewisville, TX. The man broke his legs while fleeing the rising waters.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Sat Twin Oaks Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Bexar County. A thunderstorm produced around one inch of rain in 30 minutes that filled a drainage ditch near the intersection of Hwy 281 and Bitters Rd. in northern San Antonio. A homeless man was camping in the ditch at the time and was washed away and drowned.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Whitehouse
events.description: 1 death. Smith County. A downburst affected much of the southern and eastern sections of the city of Whitehouse, resulting in numerous trees being snapped and uprooted along its path. The majority of the more significant damage occurred in an east-southeasterly direction, which began in the Willows subdivision just west of Willingham Road, where several small Bradford pear trees were snapped, and small areas of shingles were ripped from the roofs of a couple of homes with winds estimated in the range of 70-75 mph. The winds from this downburst intensified as it crossed Willingham Road, affecting several streets…

events.title: Tornado near Cedar Mills
events.description: 1 death. Grayson County. The tornado first touched down in a field near Thousand Oak Trails. It then moved through the Sherwood Oaks community, producing extensive and widespread damage to trees and homes. Multiple manufactured homes were flipped, many trees were snapped in half, and one home was moved off its foundation. The tornado then crossed Lake Texoma and moved into Marshall County Oklahoma. A total of 105 structures were damaged, 53 destroyed, and 27 sustained major damage. Maximum estimated winds in Grayson County were 130 mph. One fatality occurred in a mobile home.

events.title: Tornado near Mapleton
events.description: 1 death. Houston County. This EF2 tornado was flown by emergency management and noted a continuous damage track from the first point along Highway 21 until the final point north of Crockett. There were ten total injuries including three serious ones at a pair of mobile homes with occupants thrown into an adjacent field. At least 30 structures were severely damaged.

events.title: Flash Flood near Schemersville
events.description: 2 deaths. Bexar County. Several vehicles were swept off N Graytown Road at a low water crossing. While several persons were successfully rescued, two persons lost their lives including a 5 year old female and a 52 year old female.

events.title: Flash Flood near El Paso
events.description: 2 deaths. El Paso County. Flash flooding occurred across central El Paso with a torrent of water flowing down the mountainside near Fort Blvd and Louisiana St. There was also significant water flow down Nashville St where two deaths were reported as a wall collapsed in the basement of a house and trapped a 2 year old and her 65 year old grandmother. Atlas Avenue just north of Chapin High School also had the road buckle with slabs of pavement missing. A rainfall report at the Wyler Tramway reported 4.65 of rain in a couple of hours which caused the flash flooding.

events.title: Flash Flood near Marfa
events.description: 1 death. Presidio County. Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Marfa. Law enforcement officials announced the fatality of a gentleman who got his car swept away from flash flooding within the town of Marfa. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

events.title: Flash Flood near Biggs Afb
events.description: 1 death. El Paso County. The El Paso Police reported a large amount of mud and debris causing a road closure near Doniphan and Sunland Park Drive. The area around Paisano Drive and Executive had to be closed as well due to a large amount of water flooding the intersection. Water entered homes in parts of West El Paso as nearby drainage ponds overflowed. In addition, a 39 year old female died on the Thunderbird Trail after water rushed down the side of the mountain. By the end of the day, some locations of the city had received over 4 inches of rain in 36 hours.

events.title: Flash Flood near Garland
events.description: 1 death. Dallas County. A woman drowned after her car was surrounded by water while trying to cross Spring Creek on Holford Drive in Garland. Her car was swept downstream.

events.title: Flood near Salem
events.description: 1 death. Victoria County. Two individuals were kayaking in a drainage creek that flows to Leona Creek. Around the time of heavy rain in Victoria County, both individuals were taken downstream into a pipe culvert by the force of the flowing water. The force of the rushing water pushed one individual through the pipe and other was lodged within the pipe. The individual lodged in the pipe was transported to a local hospital where they later died.

events.title: Tornado near Carthage
events.description: 1 death. Panola County. An EF2 tornado with estimated maximum winds near 125 mph touched down again from the same supercell thunderstorm that produced the tornado near and over Lake Murvaul in Southwest Panola County, with this tornado downing and uprooting about 10 hardwood and softwood trees along Highway 59 several miles south of Carthage. The tornado intensified as it tracked parallel to FM 2517 and ripped the roof off of a single family home. The tornado's damage path widened considerably as it moved between FM 2517 and County Road 405. Security footage from a local meat processing center in the Antioch…

The Sheriff said these individuals went missing around Noon CDT on 9/9/20. The vehicle was located just off a roadway in high level and rapid moving water on FM1226 just south of County Road 266. events.title: Lightning near Temple
events.description: 2 deaths (indirect). Bell County. A couple died in an early morning house fire that fire investigators determined was started by lightning.

events.title: Lightning near Eagle Ford
events.description: 1 death. Dallas County. A 16 year old male was struck by lightning while under a tree in a yard. He died from his injuries on July 9th.

events.title: Lightning near (dal)love Fld Dallas
events.description: 1 death. Dallas County. Per hospital personnel, a 61 year old female was admitted to a hospital in Dallas on June 28th with injuries sustained from a lightning strike. She died from her injuries on July 2nd. No other information was provided or could be found.

events.title: Lightning near Amelbulk
events.description: 1 death. Jefferson County. A construction worker was building an outdoor kitchen in the Diamond D Ranch Subdivision near China when he was struck by lightning. He was hospitalized for 2 week before passing in early June.

events.title: Tornado near Onalaska
events.description: 3 deaths. Polk County. Tornado touched down on the eastern shore of Lake Livingston, just NW of Onalaska then moved SE across the town then ESE across Polk County. Some of the most significant damage was in Paradise Acres area of Onalaska. Winds possibly reached 140 mph as the storm moved across this location, which was the only EF3 damage the NWS could confirm along the 30 mile track. The tornado killed three and injured 33 in Onalaska with 291 homes affected and 46 destroyed. It was estimated to be about 500 yards wide as it moved across the town.
